what: SHA-256 of the PCM samples of Minesweeper's recorded sounds (the WAV's data chunk, i.e. the file from byte 44 on; the 44-byte header is not hashed because it carries no sound).
why: The recording itself is not committed: media files (.wav) are refused by the repository's pre-push guard, and a fixture a person can open is not needed, only a strict proof that the sounds are unchanged. Re-recorded after the font and joystick work: the binaries changed a few bytes, which moves instruction timing slightly, so a cue can begin a few samples later inside the WAV's sample windows. Measured, burst by burst, against the previous recording: starts move by 0 to 8 samples (most by 0 to 2), the recording's length is unchanged (238294 bytes), and a few sample values differ slightly because the WAV averages the machine's level over each sample's window. Note, length and peak are unchanged: every cue's pitch is within one zero crossing of where it was, its length within one sample, its peak identical (20160).
command: node cli/cloadm.js -m dragon64 --program minesweeper --frames 30 --poke $3003=$5E,$ED --type ' ' --frames 20 --wav OUT.wav --type ' ' --frames 20 --type '{RIGHT}{DOWN}F' --frames 20 --type '{UP}{RIGHT}{RIGHT}' --frames 5 --type F --frames 10 --type F --frames 10 --type ' ' --frames 60 --wav-stop
listen: To hear it, run that command with OUT.wav set to a path outside this repository (the same sequence tests/games.test.js runs). Nothing is written into the repo.
note: Phase shift is expected and documented; the sound itself is unchanged.
